prompts.prompt: Use case: identity-preserve. Input 1 is the APPROVED inventory icon of ONE specific helmet. Produce a game-equipment TURNAROUND SPRITE SHEET of precisely that helmet, preserving its recognizable construction, shapes, materials, colors and distinctive parts. It is a common equipment model for every character, not a redesign for a class. A transparent square sheet containing EXACTLY FOUR isolated helmet overlays in a strictly regular 2 by 2 grid: TOP LEFT = straight FRONT; TOP RIGHT = true BACK; BOTTOM LEFT = head turned toward viewer's LEFT, front-side three-quarter angle about 65 degrees; BOTTOM RIGHT = head turned toward viewer's RIGHT, front-side three-quarter angle about 65 degrees. For all four views the camera looks slightly down, about 15 degrees above horizontal, matching a native64 overhead-ish roguelike actor. All four are the SAME physical helmet at the SAME physical scale and with the SAME lower head/neck attachment height. Do not copy the icon's perspective to all cells. Preserve asymmetric details on their actual physical side; an optic visible on the near side of the RIGHT-facing view must be on the far/mostly hidden side of the LEFT-facing view. On the BACK show the rear shell and rear fittings, never a frontal visor. Match a deliberate economical low-resolution pixel-art style: broad pixel clusters, matte materials, restrained edge wear, clear dark contours, no microtexture, no realistic product shading. Each logical cell is 64 by 64; center each helmet around x32, lower attachment at y50, complete object within x12..52,y12..51, equal empty margin on all sides. Genuine transparent background in every gap, no frames, dividers, labels, letters, floor, cast shadow or glow halos. Only wearable equipment surface overlays: NO human head, face, skin, hair, neck, shoulders, body, stand or mannequin. Do not fill an open face aperture with black: it must be actually transparent so the actor's painted face can show. Draw only surfaces that would be in front of an inserted head; omit interior straps/ribs which would be hidden behind that head. No added props, accessories, decorative horns or symbols. Model01: very light OPEN olive and bone-white arched protection, open sparse crown ribs, thin brow band and small temple guards. No full dome or added jaw. Keep entire face opening and the openings between the near ribs transparent. No lights. Preserve the reference's three arching ribs and sparse dark straps only where they lie over the scalp, not rear straps visible through the face.
